title: Chronic Type I Interferon Signaling Promotes Helicobacter-Associated Gastric Carcinogenesis: Functional Evidence for Psmb8
content: Background/Objectives: Helicobacter-induced chronic inflammation is the major risk factor for developing gastric cancer. Identifying pathways/genes that promote Helicobacter-induced disease is critical in preventing disease progression. Our previous studies strongly suggest a role for chronic type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling in promoting gastric carcinogenesis and identified an IFN-stimulated gene (ISG), proteasome subunit beta type 8 (PSMB8) as a potential key downstream effector. Methods: Wild-type (WT) and IFN-I receptor deficient (Ifnar1-/-) mice were infected with Helicobacter felis for six months to model chronic inflammation–driven disease progression. In addition, to functionally interrogate this IFN-I-Psmb8 axis, we utilized genetically engineered gastric organoids derived from WT and Ifnar1-/- mice infected with H. felis. Results: Histopathological analysis revealed that WT mice developed pronounced epithelial atrophic gastritis and hyperplasia compared to Ifnar1-/- mice, despite comparable levels of inflammation in both groups, proving a specific role for IFN-I signaling in promoting epithelial transformation. Molecular analyses demonstrated increased expression of ISGs, cancer stem cell (CSC), and epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers in gastric tissues of WT relative to Ifnar1-/- mice. In addition, cell invasive capabilities were observed in gastric organoids from WT but not Ifnar1-/- mice. However, upon overexpression of Psmb8, Ifnar1-/- organoids exhibited invasive cellular properties. Conclusion: Our findings demonstrate that chronic IFN-I signaling promotes gastric cancer progression by driving a Psmb8-dependent invasive program in epithelial cells. These results identify Psmb8 as a key effector of IFN-driven tumorigenesis and highlight sustained IFN-I signaling as a critical driver of epithelial transformation in inflammation-associated gastric cancer.
